sources: Mare fraction: LROC global mare boundaries (Nelson et al. 2014, LPSC 45, #2861), rasterised at 0.125 deg and averaged to 0.5 deg; documented coverage 65S-65N (a few polygons reach 66.5S).

Regolith thickness: published point measurements compiled by Rajsic et al. (2026, PSJ) / Jones & Rajsic (2026) v2.0.0 (54 usable rows). The inverse-distance map (k=9, p=2) is stored but NOT used for inference because it failed leave-one-out validation; the engine uses mare/highland geometric means with log-sd 0.59/0.69.

cross_validation.note: Leave-one-out on log thickness of the 54 literature points. Points cluster at landing sites, so LOO is optimistic for unsampled regions.

decision: Use observed mare fraction; use unit-level regolith prior; do not use the interpolated thickness map (it does not beat a constant in LOO).
